newsitem.title: UK: Argos reports Xmas sales, warns on profit.
newsitem.headline: Argos reports Xmas sales, warns on profit.

text.p: British consumer goods and homeware retailer Argos Plc said on Friday that its sales in the busy 35 days up to and including Christmas Eve had risen by 4.0 percent on a like-for-like basis but on the whole, its second half sales were lower than it had expected.

Argos said that 8.0 percent like-for-like sales growth in the year to December 28, 1996, coupled with additional operating costs, meant that its full-year pretax operating profits were unlikely to exceed 140 million pounds ($236.4 million) -- the lower end of current market expectations.
The catalogue store chain said that the second half had seen a like-for like sales growth rate of just over 6.0 percent, slower than in the first half of the year.
However, furniture, textiles and leisure products continued to perform well in the half, while sales were less buoyant in toys, watches and gifts.
This created an overall effect that gross profit margin should be around 0.3 of a percentage point higher than in the same 1995 half.

"Despite this margin improvement, the effect of lower than expected sales, together with additional operating costs mentioned in the interim report, mean that full year pretax profits are unlikely to exceed the lower end (currently 140 million pounds) of market expectations," the firm said. ($1=.5922 Pound)
